plan: Queue jungle as primary. It is Xeebs's best role at 53.8% over 305 games (overall is 50.3%). Set midlane as secondary, not the other way around.
Stop queueing carry: 42.6% over 190 games is costing real VP. When auto-filled there, play the safest comfort pick, not a learning pick.
Xeebs's champion pool is 10+ heroes wide and the top three are only 41% of the games. Gold-to-Platinum climbs are almost always pool-narrowing stories: aim for 70%+ of games on the top three.
The math: Xeebs is at 375 VP; Platinum III starts at 900. The all-time peak is 692.

coachReasoning.assessment: Four straight wins on four different heroes across four different roles — Eden, Renna, Bayle and Aurora — since the Steel loss at 5 deaths against a 3 norm. The soft spot is contribution rather than survival: the Aurora jungle win finished 0/0/3 with 183 hero damage per minute against a 462 norm.
plan: On Aurora, stay attached to the fight. Repeated hits on an enemy hero summon the frost storm around her and every further hit keeps it running, so the damage only exists while Xeebs is in contact — that is the gap behind 183 hero damage per minute against a 462 norm.

Chain the Aurora setup: Boreal Sweep first for the slow, then Hoarfrost, whose ring forms around Aurora and roots on touch, so hold the ground the target has to cross. Save Cryoseism for a target who cannot walk out of the freeze before it lands.

On Bayle, press Dire Howl on the way in rather than after the damage arrives — the heal at the end of the buff is based on the damage taken while it was up. Berserk switches on by itself once Bayle drops low, so that moment is a window to keep swinging, not the cue to run; the 1/5/6 game paid 5 deaths learning that.

On Steel, spend Bull Rush on the exit as often as the entry, since Steel is unstoppable through the dash, and drop Force Shield between the enemy carry and the team so their shots stop at the wall. The Steel game was the only loss in the set, at 5 deaths against a 3 norm.

On Khaimera, keep something in melee range: damaging heroes and monsters builds Rage, and Rage makes every cooldown come back faster. Open Ambush onto a target already hurt — it hits harder the more health they are missing — follow with Unleash, and hold Invigorate to cleanse the stun that would otherwise end the fight.

insights.title: The winning stretch was a spread, not a specialty
insights.finding: The four wins came on Eden, Renna, Bayle and Aurora across carry, midlane, offlane and jungle. What is going right is not hero-specific — Eden held deaths to 4 against a 6 norm and Renna to 2, though the Bayle win still paid 5.

insights.title: Alive is not the same as useful
insights.finding: The Aurora jungle win finished 0/0/3 with 183 hero damage per minute against a 462 norm, down 60%. Zero deaths is worth little when the fight is being watched from the edge of it.

insights.title: Wards are the cheapest upgrade on the board
insights.finding: 4.7 wards per game is 56% of the squad average. For a player whose most-played role is the jungle at 305 games, that is free information being left in the shop before every objective.

insights.title: Khaimera and the jungle
insights.finding: Khaimera is a jungle fighter and holds the best record of the heroes listed at 65.7% over 166 games, and jungle is the most-played role at 305 games. Marginal games on Khaimera are priced at +3.8 wins per 100.
